Abstract                                                                                    It goes on to describe big data analytics as not just impor-
In this paper, we propose Database Processing Units, or                                     tant for business, but essential. The article emphasized that
DPUs, a class of domain-specific database processors that                                   analyses must process large volumes of a wide variety, and
can efficiently handle database applications. As a proof of                                 at real-time or nearly real-time velocity. With the big data
concept, we present the instruction set architecture, microar-                              technology and services market forecast to grow from $3.2B
chitecture, and hardware implementation of one DPU, called                                  in 2010 to $16.9B in 2015 [23], and 2.6 exabytes of data
Q100. The Q100 has a collection of heterogeneous ASIC                                       created each day [28], it is imperative for the research com-
tiles that process relational tables and columns quickly and                                munity to develop machines that can keep up with this data
energy-efficiently. The architecture uses coarse grained in-                                deluge.
structions that manipulate streams of data, thereby maxi-                                       For its part, the Database Management System (DBMS)
mizing pipeline and data parallelism, and minimizing the                                    software    community has been exploring optimizations such
need to time multiplex the accelerator tiles and spill inter-                               as  using  column    stores [1–3, 24, 27, 34], pipelining opera-
mediate results to memory. This work explores a Q100 de-                                    tions  [4, 6], and  vectorizing  operations [40], to take advan-
sign space of 150 configurations, selecting three for further                               tage  of  commodity    server hardware.
analysis: a small, power-conscious implementation, a high-                                      This work applies those same techniques, but in hard-
performance implementation, and a balanced design that                                      ware,  to construct a domain-specific processor for databases.
maximizes performance per Watt. We then demonstrate that                                    Just as  conventional DBMSs operate on data in logical enti-
the power-conscious Q100 handles the TPC-H queries with                                     ties of  tables and columns, our processor manipulates these
three orders of magnitude less energy than a state of the art                               same    data  primitives.  Like DBMSs use software pipelin-
software DBMS, while the performance-oriented design out-                                   ing  between    relational operators to reduce intermediate re-
performs the same DBMS by 70X.                                                              sults, we   too can  exploit pipelining between relational oper-

                                                                     (a) Unrestricted Graph of Spatial Instructions
2.     Q100 Instruction Set Architecture
Q100 instructions implement standard relational operators
that manipulate database primitives such as columns, tables,          4 ColSelect        2 ColFilter       2 BoolGen   1 Stitch 1 Part 2 Aggregator 2 Appender
and constants. The producer and consumer relationship be-            (b) Resource Profile
tween operators are captured with dependencies specified by
                                                                    Temporal Instruction #1
the instruction set architecture. Queries are represented as
graphs of these instructions with the edges representing data
dependencies between instructions. For execution, a query           Temporal Instruction #2

is mapped to a spatial array of specialized processing tiles,
each of which carries out one of the primitive functions.           Temporal Instruction #3
When producer-consumer node pairs are mapped to the same
temporal stage of the query, they operate as a pipeline with
data streaming direction from producer to consumer.                  (c) Resource-Aware Temporal Instructions
   The basic instruction is called a spatial instruction or
sinst. These instructions implement standard SQL-esque op-        Figure 2. The example query from Figure 1 is mapped onto

partition, and sort. Figure 1 shows a simple query written        as data dependencies. Given a set of Q100 resources, the
in SQL to produce a summary sales quantity report per sea-        graph is broken into three temporal instructions that are
son for all items shipped as of a given date. Figure 1 bottom     executed in sequence, one after another.
shows the query transformed into Q100 spatial instructions,
retaining data dependencies. Together, boolgen and colfil-

4.                 Q100 Evaluation                                                                  Although MonetDB supports multiple threads, our mea-
Taking what we have learned about the Q100 system, its                                           surements of power and speedups indicate that individ-
ISA, its implementation, and its communication both in-                                          ual TPC-H queries do not parallelize well, even for large
ternal and external, we now compare our three configura-                                         databases (i.e., 40 GB). Here we will compare the Q100’s
tions, LowPower, Pareto, and HighPerf, with a conventional                                       performance and energy to the measured single threaded
software DBMS. This evaluation takes on three parts: ini-                                        values, as well as to an optimistic estimate of a 24-way par-
tial power and performance benchmarking for the TPC-H                                            allelized software query, one that runs 24 times faster than
queries as executed on a conventional DBMS+CPU system,                                           the single threaded at the same average power as a single
comparison of Q100’s execution of TPC-H to that system’s,                                        software thread. In the upcoming comparisons, we will pro-
and finally an evaluation of how a Q100 designed for one                                         vide both the MonetDB single-thread SW and MonetDB
scale of database handles the same queries over a database                                       24-thread SW (Idealized) as reference points.
100 times larger.                                                                                   For the Q100, we use the full timing and power model,
